newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber buoyed by buying on Thai news.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber buoyed by buying on Thai news.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber was boosted at the close on Tuesday by some modest buying largely on the back of news the Thai cabinet has approved a decision to raise its support price for rubber, dealers said.
"I think there was some covering for RSS3 (grade) rubber after news on Thailand's decision came out," a dealer said.
Thailand raise its support price for RSS3 rubber to 29 baht a kg from 27.50 baht.
Dealers reacted sceptically, however, to the development, saying the rest of the market was at around 24-25 baht.
"The impact is probably going to be slight because the support price by the government is around five baht below the rest of the market," one dealer said.

One dealer said manufacturers were asking for a price of June RSS3 grade rubber at around 108.50 U.S. cents a kg, but buyers baulked at the prospect and insisted on a price of 109.00 U.S. cents a kg. "It's a two-tier market. The Thais are on one side and the rest of us in the other," one dealer said.
At 0945 GMT, June RSS3 was seen at around 109.50 U.S. cents a kg from 109.00 cents. January/March TSR20 was seen at 110.00 U.S. cents a kg from 109.25 cents. - Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
